id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

userUpdatedFields.description:
System managed field that keeps track of which fields in the seed data obj were updated by a user (as opposed to
the provisioner/authorizer).  Fields in seed data objs that are updated by users will not have those changes
overridden by provisioning.

hidden.description:
Field that marks a seed data obj as hidden.  When a seed data obj that was created via provisioning (e.g owned by
c3), user removals of that obj are handled by marking the obj as hidden to prevent future provisioning from causing
them to reappear.

userOwned.description:
A seed data entry is considered to be user owned if either this flag is true or the {@link Meta#created created}
field of {@link Persistable#meta} is not the authorizer or provisioner.  This field is completely managed by the
system.  It will be set while creating an entry if it is being created by the authorizer and the
{@link UpsertSpec#forceUserUpdate} is set to true.

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

frozen.description: If true, then the pipe shall not be retrained

trained.description: True if training has succeeded and false otherwise.

flattenInput.description: If true, the underlying model only accepts flattened input.

hyperparamOverrides.description: The hyperparameters overridden of a native model or pipe.

hyperparamSearchSpace.description:
A collection of {@link Hp.ParamSpace}s for the hyperparameters of this pipe. This search space will be used to
perform hyperparameter searches.

hpoSpec.description:
Used to provide configuration for {@link #search}. Some configurations include how to validate results, which
search algorithms will be used, and limits on execution iterations.

hpoExperiment.description: {@link Hpo.Experiment} stores the result of hyperparameter optimization to find the best model/pipeline.

experiment.description: Reference to the experiment that produced this {@link MlPipe}. For example, this could be a {@link Hpo.ExperimentBase}.

modelFiles.description:
Map of urls of saved model files
key - model file name, value - {@link Url} corresponding to model file name

customModelCode.description:
A map containing {Module Name: Compressed Source Code} key-value pairs. The module name is the name of the
module from where the source code was taken from. (i.e. numpy).

processFunc.description: Name for the function on the native model to call to do {@link MlProcessable#process}.

underlyingPipe.description:
A pipe that contains the native model and implements {@link MlAtomicPipe#doProcess} and optionally
{@link MlAtomicPipe#doTrain}. If set, the implementation of the APIs on the `MlAtomicPipe` interface will be
dispatched through the underlying pipe. Otherwise, the developer has an additional responsibility to implement the
APIs.
DEVELOPER NOTE: If sub-types of {@link MlTemplate.AtomicPipe} is designed to have `underlyingPipe`, it is required to
override {@link MlTemplate.AtomicPipe#hasUnderlyingPipe} and return `True`

lookbackDuration.description:
The lookback duration defines the period of time that the pipeline will consider for scaling purposes.
This property is important for handling historical data, enabling the model to take into account past
risk scores and adjust them according to the defined lookback window.
The duration is specified using the `Duration` type, and the value is set privately to maintain internal
consistency.

copy.description:
Flag indicating whether to scale on a copy of the input data (i.e., creating a new scaled copy),
or whether to perform scaling directly on the input data (in-place scaling).
When set to `true`, scaling is performed on a new copy of the input data, leaving the original data unchanged.
When set to `false`, scaling will modify the original input data directly.

default true

clip.description:
Flag indicating whether to clip the scaled values to the range [0, 1].
When enabled (`true`), values outside the range [0, 1] are clipped to 0 or 1 respectively, ensuring that the scaled
values stay within a defined range. This is useful in preventing extreme values that may occur due to outliers.

default true

title:
This entity defines a custom pipeline for performing Min-Max scaling of risk scores and related data.
It is part of the `ReliabilityRiskMl.RiskScoreScaling` module and extends the base `Pipe` type.
The pipeline is used to scale various input data (e.g., training features, inference features, residuals)
within the context of risk scoring and anomaly detection.

The pipeline allows the following:
- Min-Max scaling of the input features and other relevant data to the desired range (typically [0, 1]).
- Support for both training and inference modes by using the `fit()` and `transform()` functions of the Min-Max scaler.
- Option to perform scaling either in-place or on a copy of the input data.

The pipeline's primary objective is to transform data into a normalized form where the features and residuals are scaled,
and the risk score is normalized, making it suitable for downstream analysis or alert generation.

Inputs:
- `trainingFeatures`: The features used during the training phase for scaling.
- `inferenceFeatures`: The features that will be scaled during inference.
- `scaledTrainingFeatures`: The scaled version of the training features, output after scaling.
- `scaledInferenceFeatures`: The scaled version of the inference features, output after scaling.
- `residuals`: The residuals from the model output (used in anomaly detection or error assessment).
- `scaledResiduals`: The scaled version of the residuals, output after scaling.
- `reconstructions`: Reconstructed data used for comparison against the original data.
- `scaledReconstructions`: The scaled version of the reconstructed data.
- `riskScore`: The computed risk score to be normalized.
- `alertContext`: Contextual data related to any alerts generated by the risk score model.

Outputs:
- `riskScoreNormalized`: The normalized risk score after applying Min-Max scaling.

The Min-Max scaler adjusts the range of the input data to a predefined range (e.g., [0, 1]) and is used to ensure
that the input data values are within a standard range, which is especially useful for models that rely on normalized
features for effective performance.
name: ReliabilityRiskMl.RiskScoreScaling.MinMaxScalerPipe
